exposure: Practitioners' knowledge about early postpartum IUD insertion (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
Practitioners' practices of early postpartum IUD insertion
Practitioners' willingness to discuss/perform early postpartum IUD insertion
Discussions about contraception during pregnancy follow-up
outcome: Awareness of IUD insertion possibility after vaginal delivery
Awareness of IUD insertion possibility during cesarean section
Current use of early postpartum IUD insertion method
Interest in discussing early postpartum IUD insertion with patients
Interest in performing early postpartum IUD insertion after training
Frequency of systematic contraception discussions during pregnancy
cohort: The study participants were 408 obstetricians-gynaecologist professionals and midwives in France.
finding: Insertion of Intra-Uterine Devices in early postpartum is uncommon in France, primarily due to a lack of knowledge among practitioners, despite their expressed interest in adopting this practice after training.
mod_finding: The study found that 63% of practitioners knew about IUD insertion after a vaginal delivery, while only 31% knew it could be inserted during a cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Current practices and knowledge of French practitioners regarding early postpartum IUD contraception.
